strategy.summary: Leitner & Sohn is a sound, family-owned fastener house (founded 1929) supplying M12 bolt, nut and washer under a framework contract with prices fixed per calendar year. It is our cheapest source on bolt and nut by a wide margin and slightly dearer than Brucker on the washer. Its quality is far better than all alternatives, while delivery reliability sits below the contract target. It has idle capacity (second shift on hold) and wants volume, which makes the planned single-supplier kit our main trade good. Its renewal pattern is to ask modestly and settle at or near zero. The key account manager can close small moves alone; larger moves go to a pricing committee. We are a tiny customer to it, so respect and volume work, and pressure does not. Evidence is thin on cost: there is no should-cost for any part.
strategy.decision_maker: Key account manager (sales), who has his own authority for small price changes. Larger moves need the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks (doc:20260513-70610-M1). Family owners are in the background.

persona.style: relationship-oriented, cooperative; asks modestly and settles low; formal approval line for bigger moves
other_traits: cheapest source on bolt and nut versus rival
quality far better than peers and rivals
OTD below contract target, weakest on the M12 bolt
financially sound; we are a negligible customer to it
owns tooling per library (sourcing shows n/a; unclear)

needs.detail: Second shift on hold since spring; sales twice offered to take additional parts at short notice. The kit (including the M16 bolt it does not supply today) and quota shifts from Mairhofer and Brucker are what it values most.
Forecasts are rising on all parts and shared with it; it holds only a 30-50% quota today.
It wants a modest index-backed increase (fastener PPI, labour) that stays under the committee threshold.
A longer commitment or extension beyond the current term secures its restarted shift.
Long relationship (washer since 2012); unsolicited fair invitation shows it values contact.

constraints.detail: Price changes above the small threshold go to the pricing committee, adding a two-week cycle per round.
Prices are fixed per calendar year; changes need written notice before the year-end deadline. The contract auto-extends unless terminated with notice.
Low dependency on us and strong finances: it can walk away if squeezed. It is already our cheapest bolt and nut source.
Delivery reliability below the contract target, concentrated on the M12 bolt and nut. Committing it to tighter delivery may cost it.

levers.why: The kit bundle is exactly the volume its idle shift needs; present it as the opportunity it can earn with a sharp kit price and a price hold.
Rising nut volume, checkable and shared with it: volume worth more to a supplier with idle capacity.
Rising bolt volume; same logic, a fresh record for a later round if not used at opening.
Rising washer volume supports a hold or a small reduction.
Washer only: Brucker is slightly cheaper today, the one rival figure that favours us.
Acknowledge its offer to take more parts; links our volume to its spare capacity without sounding needy.
Its history of settling at zero frames any ask; use as context, not as a taunt.
Prices are fixed per year with formal notice; use if an increase is asked late or mid-year.
OTD below the contract target (above peer median): a fresh fact for a late round or to ask for a delivery commitment on the bolt.
Nut complaints, mostly certificate/marking process faults: a late filler or for a quality case.
We pay reliably; supports a fair-customer stance.
If it cites cost drivers, show the 12-month fastener index supports only about one point, far below a larger ask.
Checkable anchor for the current nut price against any increase.

trades.why: Idle capacity: binding higher quota or the kit volume is worth far more to it than to us, within our fixed need.
Planning security for restarting its shift; 24 months captures the value.
It already meets a short lead time; demanding shorter adds cost without benefit.
There is no cash need, so faster payment buys little. Test longer payment only cheaply and never alongside a price cut.
Only if it insists: the fastener index moves slowly. A clause with no deadband on that index may be acceptable at a lower base price.
Quality is already excellent; only formalise it, do not trade price for it.

price_view.reasoning: There is no should-cost. Bolt and nut are already well below the rival's price and its own RFQ quotes, so it is likely near a firm floor there. The washer has small room via Brucker's lower price. Cost drivers justify roughly a one-point rise at most, and it habitually settles at zero. The realistic goal is a price hold, a small washer cut, and a sharp kit price in exchange for volume.

do: Treat it as a valued long-term partner and our quality benchmark
Lead with the volume/kit opportunity and concrete binding volume
Keep requested moves small enough for the account manager to close without committee, or allow committee time
Bring checkable records, one fresh per round
dont: Do not threaten to terminate or move volume
Do not reveal Mairhofer's bolt or nut prices
Do not ask open questions about its costs or margin
Do not push after a final offer
Do not cite steel, copper or other market news as if it applies to it

Market news on steel and copper would hand it arguments; do not raise it
Demanding OTD improvement plus a price cut together may stall talks; trade one for the other
Hinting at kit volume without committing it makes it ask for proof and withhold credit
Asking for moves above the committee threshold adds cycles; also avoid deadlines that clash with committee timing
strategy.writer_notes: Frame every e-mail around growing the partnership: more parts, the kit, longer cover, in exchange for keeping prices stable. Use the washer rival price only for the washer. If it asks for an increase, acknowledge its labour and index pressure, then show the index supports little and offer volume or length instead of price. Step in small, real moves; respect its committee rhythm.
questions_to_ask: Which term matters most to you in return for holding prices: contract length, binding volume, or something else?
How can we time our proposal so it fits your pricing committee's schedule?

findings.text: No should-cost exists for any of the four parts, so we cannot say how far Leitner's prices sit above its full cost. The analysis rests only on index drivers, price history and rival prices, which makes it thin.

Leitner is the cheapest source we have on the M12 bolt and the M12 nut. On the bolt it charges 12.46 per 100 against Mairhofer's 14.52 (+16.5%). On the nut it charges 4.91 per 100 against Mairhofer's 5.60 (+14.1%). It also undercut Mairhofer in both 2025 benchmark RFQs (12.68 vs 14.92; 4.96 vs 5.82), yet Mairhofer was awarded both. Price room downward on these parts is likely small, and Leitner may be pricing near its floor.

On the M12 washer Leitner sits slightly above Brucker: 12.78 per 1000 against Brucker's contract price of 12.64 (-1.1%). Leitner won the 2025 RFQ even though it quoted 13.06 against Brucker's 12.80. The washer is the one part with a clear rival-based argument for a reduction of about 1%.

Cost drivers justify only a small increase if any. The fastener producer price index (PPI-C2594) rose +1.7% over 12 months, which is about +1.0 to 1.06% on price. Labour costs (LCI-C) rose +2.7%, about +0.2 to 0.35% on price. Together that is roughly +1.2 to 1.4%. The fastener index is still 1.2% below its 2023-08 peak, while prices have been flat since 2023. Steel +7.3% since January and copper +48% are market news not tied to this supplier, and copper is irrelevant to zinc-plated steel fasteners.

Leitner's price history shows no supplier-wide change since its last price round. It has held 0% for three renewals on the bolt and the nut, and the washer moved only +1.5% in 2024. It usually asks +2 to 3.6% and settles at about 0%.

Leitner has no price record for the M16 bolt (part 360011); Mairhofer supplies 100% of it at 37.64 per 100. If a kit bundle adds this part, there is no benchmark from Leitner and its quote will be fresh.

supplier_wants: Index-based increase of about +1 to 2% citing the fastener index and labour costs
Volume (it has spare capacity, with the second shift on hold)
Keep any increase under 2% to avoid its pricing committee
risks: Leitner is already the lowest price on the bolt and nut; pushing too hard risks a walk-away (financially sound, and we are a small customer to it)
Citing Mairhofer's prices would reveal that Leitner is far cheaper and weaken our position
Citing peak or all-time-high index figures is not checkable and costs trust
Leitner owns the tooling for the parts it supplies

useful_arguments.why: Brucker is 1.1% cheaper on the washer: the only part with a credible case for a reduction.
Rising nut volume is worth more to a supplier with idle capacity.
Rising M12 bolt volume can be traded for price stability.
Rising washer volume supports holding or reducing the washer price.
Idle second shift means it needs volume; a kit bundle gives it that volume in exchange for price.
It habitually settles at 0%, which anchors any ask.
Current nut price anchors the negotiation.
Prices are fixed per calendar year and changes need 90 days' notice.
The planned single-supplier kit gives volume leverage across all four parts.
We pay reliably, which supports our standing as a fair customer.

findings.text: Decision structure: the key account manager can only move up to 2 % on price on his own. Anything above 2 % goes to a pricing committee that meets every two weeks. Asks of 2 % or less can close quickly; larger moves add a two-week cycle per round. Keep concessions we request, or increases we accept, within the 2 % band so the counterpart can close without escalation.

Spare capacity and hunger for volume: sales told us twice (April and May 2026) that they could take additional parts at short notice. The second shift has been on hold since spring. They need volume to refill capacity, which makes the one-supplier kit (about 30,000 kits a year; 360010/011/012/030) highly attractive to them. Note that they do not supply 360011 today; Mairhofer holds it at 100 %.

Financially sound, family-owned, long-established company (founded 1929, 280 staff, EUR 139 M turnover, 30 % equity ratio, credit index 179 and unchanged, VDA 6.3 A). There is no financial stress to exploit. Our spend of about EUR 40k is negligible to them, so goodwill and the volume upside matter more than any threat.

Relationship-oriented style: they sent an unsolicited trade fair invitation, and the relationship is long (360030 since 2012). In past renewals they asked for +1.2 % to +3.6 % and settled at +0.0 % almost every time. They concede readily when they get respect and arguments.

Weak spots in their position. Their prices are already well below the rivals' (Mairhofer is +14 % to +16.5 % on 360010/360012), so they cannot credibly claim to be uncompetitive, and we must not reveal that gap. On 360030, Brucker is 1.1 % cheaper.

We are a good payer by their standards: on average only 2.1 days late, never more than 10 days late, and no discounts or short payments. Payment terms are 30 days against our standard of 60, so faster payment is not much of a lever for them to ask for.

Inclusion of 360011 and a single-source kit award
Price changes kept at or below 2 % to avoid the committee, or a modest increase backed by PPI/labour
A longer commitment that keeps the relationship stable

findings.text: Framework contract ctr:4600070610 covers M12 bolt, nut and washer (not the M16 bolt part:360011). Prices are fixed per calendar year. A change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, so by about 2 Oct for the following 1 January. A rise notified after that date cannot take effect until the next year. Payment is 30 days net (our standard is 60), delivery DAP with a 5-day lead time, OTD target 95% and EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint.

The term runs to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice, i.e. by 2027-04-01. That exit is still open but is a real option only if we will use it; threats have not worked in practice.

History of 9 annual renewals: it asked +1.2% to +3.6% and settled 0% in 8 of them. The one exception was the washer in 2023, asked +3.2%, settled +1.5%. Prices are flat since 2023 (bolt 12.46/100, nut 4.91/100, washer 12.59 rising to 12.78/1000). Asks above 2% need its pricing committee, which meets every two weeks, so expect its opening asks to cluster near that line and allow time for approval.

Dual sourcing gives us real alternatives on all three of its parts:
- Bolt M12: Mairhofer holds 60% and quotes and is paid 14.52/100, which is +16.5% versus Leitner.
- Nut: Mairhofer holds 70% at 5.60/100, which is +14.1%.
- Washer: Brucker holds 50% at 12.64/1000, which is -1.1%.
So Leitner is the cheap source on bolt and nut. Revealing rival prices there helps them, not us. Only the washer rival price favours us. Leitner won the 2025 washer benchmark RFQ; Mairhofer won the bolt and nut benchmarks.

Mutual dependency is low. Our spend is about EUR 40k a year, roughly 0.03% of its EUR 139M turnover, and its finances are sound (equity 30%, credit index stable, audit A). It can walk away; we are a small customer. Tooling owner is shown as n/a in sourcing, although the argument library says it owns tooling. For standard ISO parts the switching cost is likely low; this needs checking.

Opportunity: it has spare capacity (second shift on hold since spring) and offers to take additional parts at short notice. We plan a single-supplier kit of about 30,000 kits a year, including part:360011, which today is 100% Mairhofer. Forecast volumes are rising 6-15%. Bundling volume plus an extension would be a trade that gives it what it needs.

supplier_wants: Annual price increase in roughly the 1-2% range, justified by fastener PPI +1.7% and labour +2.7%
Higher and binding volume / larger quota to fill idle second-shift capacity
Possibly an index clause on PPI fasteners

findings.text: Delivery is the weak spot: rolling OTD 88.6% (requested = confirmed) vs contract target 95%, flat around 86-89% for two years, slight recovery from 86.4% a year ago. Late lines average about 10 days late (max 24). Above the peer median 84.6%, so it's a fair point but not a crushing one.

OTD gap is concentrated on the M12x40 bolt (82.1% on time, 17.9% late) and the M12 nut (88.5%, up to 24 days late); the washer is at 96%. The bolt is also where the rival Mairhofer holds 60% quota, so its delivery record matters most there.

Quality is strong and argues its case: 68 ppm rolling vs peer median 457 ppm, 0 overdue 8Ds, class A green, VDA 6.3 A. The alternative sources run 334-400 ppm on the same parts (Mairhofer 400 ppm on 360010, 174 on 360012; Brucker 334 on 360030). Ppm rose in 2026Q2 (85) from a low of 54 in 2025Q4, now 68 - a slight uptick, not a trend reversal.

Complaints are small but recurring: 19 supplier-caused QNs in the last 12 months. The most frequent causes are wrong material certificate and missing marking, which are documentation/process faults. The nut is worst (8 complaints, EUR 1,050 recharged). All 8Ds are closed. Costs per complaint are low, at EUR 150 flat, so this is a talking point rather than a large cost.

Volume outlook is up on all three parts, and the forecasts are shared with the supplier: bolt 574k vs 541k ordered, nut 654k vs 600k, washer 736k vs 677k. A planned kit bundle would add the M16 bolt (208k, today 100% with Mairhofer). The supplier has idle capacity (second shift on hold), so extra volume is a real trade good.

Prices have been flat since 2023 (washer +1.5% in 2024). It is far cheaper than the rivals on the bolt (-14%) and the nut (-12%), but slightly dearer on the washer than Brucker (12.78 vs 12.64). Our order behaviour is clean: no stale lines, few rush lines on the bolt and nut.

Faster payment than 30 days net or keep it
Binding volume / longer commitment to fill the idle second shift
Kit bundle volume including M16 bolt

arguments.text: We are already your cheapest source by a wide margin on bolt and nut and have held prices flat for four years despite asking each year. Our M12 bolt at 12.46/100 against Mairhofer's 14.52 (about 14 % below), and our nut at 4.91/100 against 5.60 (about 12 % below). There is no room left to cut; if anything a modest catch-up is fair.

Our quality is in a different league. Our last-12-month ppm is 56 / 100 / 59 on bolt, nut and washer, against Mairhofer's 400 and 174 and Brucker's 334. On a total-cost view our parts cost you far less in complaints, sorting and line stops. That is worth a price premium, not a discount.

Our costs are genuinely rising. Fastener producer prices are up 1.7 % in 12 months, manufacturing labour costs are up 2.7 %, and basic steel is up 7.3 % since January. After four years at zero, an increase of around 1.5-2 % is moderate.

We offer the shortest lead time (5 days versus 7-8 days), a contract that auto-extends, and a family firm with a 30 % equity ratio and a stable credit index. We are a secure partner for the planned kit.
On the washer, Brucker's price is only about 1 % lower, and their quality is about 5x worse. You awarded us the 2025 washer benchmark.

weak_points: Our on-time delivery is 88.6 % against a 95 % contract target, and the M12 bolt is at only 82 %.
The second shift has been on hold since spring and we told them twice that we have spare capacity. They know we need volume.
Hollerau is tiny for us (about 40k EUR on 139 M EUR turnover), and they know we usually settle at 0 %.
They know that moves above 2 % need our pricing committee, and that the KAM can close small moves alone.
Our washer price is above Brucker's 12.64.
Energy prices are down 43 % versus 2022, which undercuts cost arguments.
We have no cost breakdown we want to disclose.
wants: The whole kit, including the M16 bolt (part:360011) and full quotas on bolt, nut and washer, which would fill the second shift.
A binding annual volume based on the shared forecasts (about 574k / 654k / 736k / 208k pieces).
A longer contract term, for example 24-36 months beyond 2027-06.
Payment terms kept at 30 days or shorter, and prompt payment (they currently pay about 2 days late on average).
Delivery measured against realistic confirmed dates rather than a tighter OTD penalty.
Optionally, a fastener PPI index clause instead of a fixed price.
red_lines: No price cuts on bolt or nut below current levels without a volume gain.
No washer cut below about 12.64 unless we get the full washer volume.
No sharp kit price without a binding volume and term.
No longer payment terms than 30 days.
No higher chargeback per complaint or ppm penalties that are unrealistic for our delivery performance.
No multi-year fixed price without an index or a reopener.
red_team.opening: Thank the customer for a long partnership, going back to 2012 on the washer. Point out four years of flat prices and our best-in-class quality. Request a moderate adjustment of about 2.5 % on bolt and nut and about 1.5 % on the washer, citing PPI, labour and steel. Signal immediately that we are very interested in supplying the complete kit, including the M16 bolt, and that we would review the pricing favourably in return for full quotas, a binding volume and a 3-year term.

rebuttals.answer: You are right that your bolt and nut prices have been competitive and stable, and we value that. Stability has also been the shared result of each renewal: the prices we pay today are the anchor both sides agreed. Being competitive is not by itself a reason to catch up. What we can offer is more of the business at these prices: our forecasts on all parts are rising, and the planned kit would bring you parts you do not supply today.

We agree your quality is excellent; it is the main reason we see you as the natural partner for the kit. Quality is already part of the agreement you signed, and the complaints that still occur are recharged under it, so we see it as the expected standard rather than a premium. We would rather reward it with more volume and a longer commitment than with a higher unit price.

We accept that the fastener index and labour costs have moved up, and we have checked both. Weighted by their share of the part cost, they support well under the increase you mention. Basic steel is a broader market figure than the fastener producer index, which already reflects your input materials, and energy has moved strongly in the other direction. Additional volume on your existing lines would offset a small cost rise better than a price increase.
Your short lead time and financial strength are real strengths and matter for the kit. A kit commitment would need that gap closed. We would like to build both together, with volume in return.

You won the washer benchmark and we value the long relationship on this part. Today we do buy the same washer at a slightly lower price from the second source. So on the washer a hold is the least we would expect, and a small step toward that level would strengthen your case for the larger kit share.

press: You mentioned you could take on additional parts at short notice; we would like to explore how the kit volume could fill that capacity at today's prices.
We would like to keep our proposal within what you can approve directly, so it can be settled without extra approval cycles.
On the washer we would welcome a step toward the level we pay our second source.
We note that energy costs have eased considerably, and we hope this balances part of the cost pressure you describe.
